stories.headline: Israel's election ends in a near-deadlock, exit polls show
body: Exit polls give Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 52 or 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, slightly ahead of Netanyahu's camp.
Neither side is near the 61 seats needed to govern, though Netanyahu's Likud is still the biggest single party.
Turnout was the highest in decades, and weeks of coalition talks are likely while Netanyahu stays on as caretaker.
stories.joke: Both sides claim victory. The maths claims a sequel.
stories.vc: A long caretaker period means policy limbo for Israel's defence-tech and cyber startups, which rely on government contracts.

stories.headline: A one-town ceasefire in Ukraine opens the way for aid
body: A local ceasefire began early Tuesday around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine, so an aid mission can enter.
US first lady Melania Trump led the talks with civilian negotiators from both sides, her office says.
Missile attacks resumed on Kyiv, and wider US-brokered peace talks are expected next month.
stories.vc: Small humanitarian deals are often the test runs for bigger ceasefires, which markets watch for any sign of a rebuilding boom.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, the fastest ever
body: More than 10,000 people have been infected in the Democratic Republic of Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.
It is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record and the largest ever by area.
At the same stage of the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, about 4,000 people had been infected.
stories.vc: Outbreaks like this pull funding toward vaccines, rapid tests and cold-chain logistics in Africa.

stories.headline: Bengaluru loses 43 lakh voters in the electoral roll clean-up
body: Bengaluru's electorate has shrunk from 1.03 crore to 59.08 lakh after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists.
More than 43 lakh names were removed, the most of any area in Karnataka.
Nearly half of all notices issued across the state during the checks were in Bengaluru.
stories.joke: Bengaluru traffic is still the same. Apparently the voters were the ones who left.
stories.vc: A smaller roll changes the maths for the city's coming civic polls and how parties court Bengaluru's voters.

stories.headline: Sarvam signs a deal to bring AI to India's armed forces
body: Bengaluru AI startup Sarvam signed an agreement with the Defence Ministry to work on AI for the Army, Navy and Air Force.
It covers AI applications, research, training and decision support.
It is Sarvam's first move into defence, as the government pushes homegrown defence tech.
stories.joke: Next up: a chatbot that replies 'Yes, sir' in 22 languages.
stories.vc: Government contracts give Indian AI labs steady revenue and a strong 'sovereign AI' story for investors.

stories.headline: SoftBank keeps selling Ola Electric shares
body: SoftBank sold 5.55 crore Ola Electric shares between January and October, cutting its stake to 11.7% from 12.9%.
It also sold 1.12 crore rights entitlements in Ola's nearly ₹1,000 crore rights issue.
Ola is raising money to repay debt as its revenue and market share fall.
stories.joke: When your biggest backer is quietly heading for the exit, it's not a scooter problem.
stories.vc: Early investors trimming stakes tells the market they see limited upside, which weighs on the share price and future fundraising.

stories.headline: China's AI stock boom wipes out $2.4 trillion
body: Chinese stock markets have lost about $2.4 trillion since May as worries grow about the AI race with the US.
Shanghai's tech-heavy STAR 50 index has fallen 40% since June, and other major indexes are down about 20%.
AI stocks make up over 40% of market value in China and Hong Kong, Goldman Sachs says.
stories.joke: Turns out 'beat America at AI' isn't a profit forecast.
stories.vc: If AI valuations crack in China, investors will ask whether US AI prices rest on firmer ground. Profits will decide it.

stories.headline: Disruptive raises a $10 billion fund for big AI and defence bets
body: Dallas-based Disruptive raised $10 billion to back at least 10 companies, mainly in AI and defence.
It is among the year's biggest venture funds and the largest ever raised in Texas.
The firm, founded by Alex Davis in 2012, is known for backing Groq and ElevenLabs.
stories.joke: Ten companies, ten billion. Easy maths, scary cheques.
stories.vc: Fewer, bigger bets is the new VC model for capital-hungry AI; it leaves less room for small early-stage cheques.

stories.headline: Re:Build, the factory startup behind Slate Auto, raises $2.1B
body: Massachusetts-based Re:Build, which spun out EV maker Slate Auto, raised $2.1 billion led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase.
It will use the money to make more hard-tech products and start new industrial companies.
Investors are pouring money into US manufacturing as a hedge against China.
stories.joke: America wants to make things again. Step one: raise $2 billion.
stories.vc: 'Reshoring' is now a funded category; factory-as-a-service startups could pull Indian component suppliers into US supply chains too.

stories.headline: General Compute raises $100M as 'neocloud' fears grow
body: AI cloud startup General Compute raised a $100 million Series A, renting out computing power built on specialised inference chips.
It comes as rival CoreWeave's stock hits a 12-month low and Elon Musk predicts many such clouds will die.
Its CEO says the fears are overblown and demand for compute is still huge.
stories.joke: Everyone says the bubble's popping. He says: here's $100 million.
stories.vc: Inference, running AI models rather than training them, is where steady cloud demand is shifting.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO buyers will get little say over the company
body: Anthropic's filing shows public shareholders will have little control over big decisions, including who sits on its board.
It is a public benefit company, a for-profit legally allowed to weigh its AI safety mission alongside profit.
Founder-control setups are common in tech, but TechCrunch calls Anthropic's unusually complex.
stories.joke: You can buy the stock. You just can't tell it what to do. Like a cat.
stories.vc: Investors usually discount shares with weak voting rights; Anthropic is betting its growth outweighs that.
